sides.label: A
sides.quote: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

title: No carved images to worship

text: KJV Exodus 20:4: “Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.” KJV Exodus 20:5: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;” KJV Exodus 20:6: “And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.”
scope: Lists what the text commands. It does not rule on whether or how the commandment applies today, and it adds no finding about the passage.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.

title: Do not take the name in vain
summary: The LORD’s name is not to be taken in vain; the text says he will not hold the person guiltless.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

title: Remember the Sabbath day
summary: Work six days and keep the seventh as the LORD’s Sabbath. Household, servants, animals, and the stranger inside the gates rest too. Exodus grounds it in creation.
text: KJV Exodus 20:8: “Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.” KJV Exodus 20:9: “Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:” KJV Exodus 20:10: “But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:” KJV Exodus 20:11: “For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.”
scope: Lists what the text commands. It does not rule on whether or how the commandment applies today, and it adds no finding about the passage. Deuteronomy gives a different stated reason (deliverance from Egypt). This record does not compare the two.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

sides.quote: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

title: Seek first the kingdom; take no thought for tomorrow
summary: Do not worry about food, drink, or clothing. Seek first God’s kingdom and righteousness, and do not worry about tomorrow.
text: KJV Matthew 6:31: “Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?” KJV Matthew 6:32: “(For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.” KJV Matthew 6:33: “But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.” KJV Matthew 6:34: “Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.”
scope: Lists what the text commands. It does not rule on whether or how the commandment applies today, and it adds no finding about the passage.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

title: Judge not
summary: Do not judge, or you will be judged by the same measure. Remove the beam from your own eye before the mote from your brother’s.
text: KJV Matthew 7:1: “Judge not, that ye be not judged.” KJV Matthew 7:2: “For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.” KJV Matthew 7:3: “And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?” KJV Matthew 7:4: “Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?” KJV Matthew 7:5: “Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.”
scope: Lists what the text commands. It does not rule on whether or how the commandment applies today, and it adds no finding about the passage.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

title: Ask, seek, knock
summary: Jesus tells his hearers to ask, seek, and knock, with the stated assurance that the Father gives good things to those who ask.
text: KJV Matthew 7:7: “Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:” KJV Matthew 7:8: “For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.” KJV Matthew 7:9: “Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?” KJV Matthew 7:10: “Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?” KJV Matthew 7:11: “If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?”
scope: Lists what the text commands. It does not rule on whether or how the commandment applies today, and it adds no finding about the passage.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

title: Do to others what you would have them do to you
summary: Do to others what you would have them do to you; Jesus says this sums up the law and the prophets.
text: KJV Matthew 7:12: “Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.”
scope: Lists what the text commands. It does not rule on whether or how the commandment applies today, and it adds no finding about the passage.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

title: The great commandment
summary: Asked which commandment is greatest, Jesus names love for God with heart, soul, and mind, and a second, love for your neighbor as yourself. He says all the law and the prophets hang on these two.
text: KJV Matthew 22:37: “Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.” KJV Matthew 22:38: “This is the first and great commandment.” KJV Matthew 22:39: “And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” KJV Matthew 22:40: “On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.”
scope: Lists what the text commands. It does not rule on whether or how the commandment applies today, and it adds no finding about the passage.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
